text: 🌿 The greatness of the Vinayaka vratam, as told by Suta Maharshi
Long ago, Dharmaraja lost his kingdom and all his wealth, and was living in the forest with Draupadi and his brothers.
One day he came to Naimisharanya.
There he saw Suta Maharshi, who was explaining many secrets of the puranas to Shaunaka and the other sages, and bowed to him.
“Maharshi… we have lost our kingdom and all our wealth.
If there is a vratam by which these troubles would leave us and our former glory return, please tell us,” he prayed.
Then Suta Maharshi began to tell Dharmaraja the greatness of the Sri Vinayaka vratam.
🐘 Gajasura's penance — the boon Lord Shiva gave
Long ago there was a demon named Gajasura.
He performed a terrible penance for Lord Shiva.
Pleased with his penance, Shiva appeared and said, “Gajasura… ask for whatever boon you wish.”
Gajasura bowed to Shiva and asked, “Lord… may you always dwell within my stomach.”
Unable to refuse a devotee's wish, Shiva entered Gajasura's stomach.
❤️ The plan Sri Hari made to bring Shiva back
In Kailasa, Parvati Devi did not know where Shiva was.
However much she searched, he could not be found.
At last she learned that Shiva was inside Gajasura's stomach.
Not knowing how to bring him out, she prayed to Sri Mahavishnu.
Vishnu reassured Parvati Devi and called Brahma and the other gods.
Then a plan was thought of.
Nandi, Shiva's mount, was decorated as a performing bull.
Brahma and the other gods took up instruments.
Sri Mahavishnu himself became the one leading the bull troupe, and together they all went to Gajasura's kingdom.
Before Gajasura they made Nandi dance most wonderfully.
Watching that performance Gajasura was delighted and said, “Ask for whatever you want.
I will give it.”
Then Sri Hari said, “This bull is no ordinary one.
This is Nandi, Shiva's mount.
He has come searching for his lord.
Give Shiva back.”
At those words Gajasura understood that the one before him was Sri Mahavishnu.
He realised that his death was certain.
Then, praying to the Shiva within his own stomach, he asked, “Lord… let my head be worshipped in all three worlds.
Let my hide be worn by you.”
Shiva granted that boon.
Nandi tore open Gajasura's stomach with his horns, and Shiva came out.
Then Shiva set out for Kailasa.
🌺 How the boy Parvati Devi made became Gajanana
Learning that Shiva was returning, Parvati Devi was very glad.
As she was preparing to bathe, from the turmeric paste applied to her body she shaped the form of a small boy, and with her own power gave him life.
She stood the boy at the door and said, “Until I say so, let no one come inside.”
As his mother had told him, the boy stood guard there.
Just then Shiva reached Kailasa.
As he went to step inside, the boy stopped him.
The boy did not know who stood before him.
He knew only one thing — that his mother's word must be kept.
However much Shiva said, the boy would not give way.
In a surge of anger Shiva severed the boy's head with his trident and went inside.
A little later, while speaking with Parvati Devi, the matter of the boy came up.
Learning what had happened, Parvati Devi grieved deeply.
Shiva remembered the boon he had given Gajasura.
He brought Gajasura's head, set it on the boy's body, and gave him life again.
And so that boy became Gajanana.
Parvati and Parameshwara raised him as their own son with great love.
Gajanana took as his mount a mouse named Anindya.
Afterwards Kumaraswamy was born to Parvati and Parameshwara.
👑 How Gajanana became the lord of obstacles
One day the gods and sages came to Shiva and asked, “Please appoint a lord over obstacles.”
Both Gajanana and Kumaraswamy wished for that place.
Then Shiva set a test.
“Whichever of you bathes in all the sacred rivers of the three worlds and comes back to me first shall be the lord of obstacles,” he said.
Kumaraswamy at once set off on his peacock mount.
Gajanana, however, bowed to his father and asked, “Father… how can I travel to all those rivers so quickly?
Show me a way.”
Then Shiva explained to him the greatness of the Narayana mantra and gave him its initiation.
Gajanana chanted that mantra with devotion.
A wonder happened.
Whichever sacred river Kumaraswamy reached… Gajanana was already there before him.
In the end, by the time Kumaraswamy returned to Kailasa, Gajanana was already beside Shiva.
Understanding his elder brother's greatness, Kumaraswamy bowed and said, “My brother alone is worthy of this lordship.”
And so, on the day of Bhadrapada Shuddha Chavithi, Gajanana became the lord of obstacles.
From then on he became Vighneshwara.
🌙 The moon's laughter — Parvati Devi's curse
In the joy of his becoming lord of obstacles, the gods and devotees offered Vinayaka many kudumulu, undrallu, fruits, panakam and vadapappu as naivedyam.
Vinayaka received them happily.
Some he ate… some he gave to his mouse… and some he carried in his hand as he reached Kailasa.
He bent to bow to his parents.
But with his stomach so full, bending became difficult.
The moon, seated on Shiva's head, saw that sight and laughed mockingly.
The moment the moon's glance fell on him, Vinayaka's stomach burst, all the kudumulu he had eaten came out… and Vinayaka lost his life.
Seeing her son in that state, Parvati Devi in her grief cursed the moon.
“Because of your glance my son has come to this.
From now on, whoever looks at you will suffer false blame,” she said.
Afterwards Brahma came to Kailasa with the other gods, gave Vinayaka life again, and prayed to Parvati Devi to take back the curse she had given the moon.
Parvati Devi was glad that her son had come back to life.
And so she lessened the severity of the curse on the moon.
She said, “Only on this one day on which my son died by the moon's glance — the day of Bhadrapada masam, Shukla Chavithi — will this curse fall on those who look at the moon.”
From then on people began to keep the custom of not looking at the moon on Vinayaka Chavithi.
Some time passed this way.
🦚 The false blame that came upon Sri Krishna in Dwapara Yuga
In the Dwapara Yuga, on one Vinayaka Chavithi day, Devarshi Narada came to Dwaraka to see Sri Krishna.
As evening was falling, Narada said, “Lord, today is Vinayaka Chavithi.
One must not look at the moon,” and having explained the whole account to Krishna, he left.
Krishna too had it proclaimed through Dwaraka that no one should look at the moon.
That night, without looking towards the sky, Krishna went to the cowshed.
There, as the milk was being drawn… the moon's reflection appeared in the milk.
“Alas… what blame is about to come upon me!”
Krishna thought.
💎 The Syamantaka jewel goes missing — the accusation against Krishna
Some time later Satrajit obtained a wonderful jewel by the grace of Suryadeva.
That was the Syamantaka jewel.
It had a boundless brilliance.
Satrajit wore it and came to Dwaraka.
Krishna suggested it would be good to give that jewel to the king.
But Satrajit did not agree.
Some days later Satrajit's brother Prasena put the jewel round his neck and went hunting.
In the forest a lion killed Prasena and took the jewel.
Jambavanta killed that lion and carried the jewel to his cave.
There he gave it to his daughter Jambavati as a plaything.
But in Dwaraka no one knew what had really happened.
When Prasena did not return, Satrajit accused him: “In anger at not being given the jewel, Krishna himself killed my brother and took the Syamantaka jewel.”
That word spread through all of Dwaraka.
Then Krishna remembered the moon's reflection he had seen in the milk on Vinayaka Chavithi day.
🐾 Krishna goes seeking the truth, to clear the blame upon him
To clear the blame that had come upon him, Krishna himself went to the forest to seek the truth.
There he found Prasena's body.
Near it were a lion's footprints.
Following them he found the dead lion.
From there a bear's footprints appeared.
Those footprints led to a mountain cave.
Leaving his retinue outside, Krishna went in alone.
There… was the Syamantaka jewel.
It was with Jambavati, as a plaything.
As Krishna went to take the jewel she began to cry.
Hearing that sound Jambavanta came.
Not knowing that it was Krishna before him, he entered into battle.
⚔️ The moment Jambavanta recognised his Sri Rama in Krishna
A terrible battle went on between Krishna and Jambavanta for twenty-eight days.
At last Jambavanta's strength waned.
Then one thing became clear to him.
“There can be no one but Sri Rama who could drain my strength like this!”
He realised that the Krishna standing before him was the Sri Rama of the Treta Yuga.
At once he bowed to Krishna.
Offering the Syamantaka jewel, he asked him also to marry his daughter Jambavati.
Krishna agreed.
❤️ The truth came out — the false blame was lifted
Krishna returned to Dwaraka with the Syamantaka jewel.
Before everyone he explained what had happened.
He proved that the blame laid on him was untrue.
Satrajit realised his mistake and was deeply pained.
He asked Krishna's forgiveness.
He gave his daughter Satyabhama to Krishna in marriage.
He wished to offer the Syamantaka jewel to Krishna as well.
But Krishna said, “I have no need of this jewel,” and gave it back to Satrajit himself.
And so the false blame that had come upon Krishna was lifted.
🌙 What to do if you happen to see the moon by mistake
Then the gods and sages asked Krishna: “Lord… you are capable, and so you cleared the blame that came upon you.
But what of ordinary people?”
Then Sri Krishna told them a way.
Those who happen to see the moon by mistake on Bhadrapada Shuddha Chavithi should worship Vinayaka with devotion, hear the story of the Syamantaka jewel, and place the puja akshatas on their head.
He gave the assurance that the fault of false blame is then removed.
On this occasion this shloka too is recited:
siṃhaḥ prasenam avadhīt
siṃho jāmbavatā hataḥ ।
sukumāraka mā rodīḥ
tava hyeṣa syamantakaḥ ॥
🙏 Suta Maharshi's final counsel to Dharmaraja
Having told all this, Suta Maharshi said to Dharmaraja, “You too should keep the Sri Vinayaka vratam with devotion.
Your obstacles will go and victory will come to you.”
Dharmaraja duly worshipped Vinayaka and kept the vratam.
In time he overcame his troubles and regained his kingdom.
And so the Sri Varasiddhi Vinayaka vratam, which removes obstacles and grants success, has continued from generation to generation.
🙏 oṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ
🙏 Victory to Sri Varasiddhi Vinayaka Swami
